A frame from a feature film set in 1920s New York: RUST drives and MARINE rides beside him in the open front of a black 1920s touring car, swerving down a narrow tenement street. The camera is mounted on the car's bonnet looking back at them, 35mm lens, so both men fill the frame from the chest up, faces turned to the lens in three-quarter. The masks and suits are exactly as in the attached reference image, the masks copied exactly from the close-ups: on each man the small red triangle sits over his left eye, on the right side of the picture. RUST grips the wheel in both black-gloved hands; MARINE braces one gloved hand flat on the dashboard. Just past MARINE's shoulder, soft and close, a green-painted fruit cart tips sideways and a few oranges hang in the air, a policeman in a dark tunic leaping clear behind it. Low afternoon sun slants down the street from one side, warm on brick and laundry lines, the cab half in shadow. Shot on 35mm motion-picture film, fine grain, 16:9.

Thanks.
